chunks: Yūnus narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said:
Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: “The prescribed penalty concerning wine applies when some of it or much of it is drunk.”

He said, then he said: “ʿUmar was brought Qudāmah ibn Maẓʿūn after he had drunk wine, and the proof had been established against him. So he consulted ʿAlī عليه السلام, and he ordered that he be struck eighty lashes. Then Qudāmah said: O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, there is no prescribed penalty upon me; I am among the people of this verse.”
“There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have consumed.”
He said: So ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “You are not among its people. The food of its people is lawful for them; they do not eat or drink except what Allah has made lawful for them.”
Then ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “Indeed, when the drinker drinks, he does not know what he eats or what he drinks, so flog him with eighty lashes.”

key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةُ: the legal proof or evidentiary establishment of the offense
key_terms.الْخَمْرِ: wine or intoxicating drink subject to legal prohibition
key_terms.ثَمَانِينَ: eighty, referring here to the number of lashes

ai.seo_question: Does the hadd for drinking wine apply even if only a small amount is consumed?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes that the hadd for drinking wine applies whether the amount consumed is small or large. It also clarifies that the Qur'anic verse about there being no blame for what believers consumed does not apply to consuming what Allah has made haram. The report further presents Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام affirming the legal penalty of eighty lashes for wine-drinking.
